topic: High-reputation player-founded gang chapters, permanent posse roster, Chapter Boombox home recovery, and provider-agnostic mob archetypes
requirements_locked: At high configurable gang reputation, award a gang-specific Chapter Boombox tied to stable gang_id.
Each gang may have a custom Chapter Boombox model/name/skin, e.g. a Mooshroom Shroom Box, implemented as data-driven presentation over one safe base contract.
Placing the earned Chapter Boombox at a player-selected base creates a bounded player-founded chapter with roughly five permanent named/interactable roster members by default.
Permanent residents use stable crew_member_id roster identity separate from runtime entity UUID/body identity.
Residents can be named and recruited/dismissed as followers in the player's posse while non-followers stay on the low-frequency Hangout Brain.
The Chapter Boombox is the crew home/spawn anchor. Killed/defeated permanent members enter recovery and return there after a delay only when the home chunk is naturally loaded; no force-loading.
Recovery preserves JetSetCraft-owned name, role, gang, gear/cosmetics, posse assignment, and memories while preventing equipment/inventory duplication and infinite source-mob loot farming.
Semantic mob_archetype_id is separate from concrete provider entity_type_id so concepts such as Mooblooms can survive backport/provider changes.

Mob archetype resolution uses explicit tags/server overrides, curated aliases, normalized registry/name synonyms, safe trait evidence, and modpack aliases; uncertain matches remain dormant instead of being guessed.
Multiple providers resolve deterministically and never randomly change an already-living member's provider.
If a provider disappears, roster identity remains; a later safe spawn/recovery may bind another provider for the same archetype without fabricating absent provider-specific NBT.
All of the above retains the standalone compatibility covenant: no vanilla/mod class replacement, no worldgen takeover, no forced chunk tickets.
